title: Simultaneous spatiotemporal computational super-resolution and multi-parametric fluorescence microscopy
protocol: Use the appropriate microscopy setup and camera.
Adjust magnification using the slider if higher magnification is required.
Use the dual-emission image splitter for dual channel measurements.
Excite the sample with suitable laser powers: 100-300 µW for 488 nm excitation, and 0.1-1 mW for 561 nm excitation when using an EMCCD with EM gain of 300.
Record a stack of images at high temporal resolution: use 1,000 frames per second (fps) for bilayer measurements and 500 fps for cell membrane measurements.
Increase recording rates if sufficient signal-to-noise ratio is achievable.
Operate the Andor Solis EMCCD in kinetic mode with baseline clamp to minimize baseline fluctuation.
Set pixel readout speed to 10 MHz, analog-to-digital gain to maximum at 4.7, and vertical shift speed to 0.45 µs.
Use an EM gain of 300 for the Andor Solis EMCCD setup.
Operate sCMOS with a pixel readout rate of 200 MHz in overlap readout mode.
Use rolling electronic shuttering mode and 12-bit dynamic range for sCMOS.
Save the image stack as a 16-bit tiff image stack.
Perform spatial or temporal binning based on SNR for imaging FCS.
Use 1×1 binning or 2×2 binning depending on the pixel size and detector type.
Generate and fit the plot with spatial binning of 1×1 to 5×5 based on SNR.
Time-bin data to at least 10 ms per frame for N&B analysis.
Use higher time binning of 20 ms for better background differentiation in intensity thresholding.
Perform time binning to 200 ms per frame for computational super-resolution microscopy.
Temporally bin all frames to obtain a single time-averaged image for deconvolution.
Load the bilayer measurement file into the ImFCS plugin in ImageJ.
Set the appropriate values for frame time, correlator (p, q), pixel size, NA, and λ₁ in the plugin.
Compute and display a plot of diffusion coefficient values for various PSF and binning combinations.
Load the image stacks in the ImFCS 1.52 plugin.
Set the appropriate values for frame time, correlator (p, q), pixel size, NA, λ₁, and bleach correction in the plugin.
Calculate ACFs with a suitable diffusion model.
Fit the data using available filters to exclude outliers or non-converged fits.
Generate and fit the diffusion law plot with a straight line for square binning of desired range.
Temporally bin the image stack in ImageJ using the Image → Transform → Bin command sequence.
Set the desired X, Y, and Z shrink factor and choose the Sum bin method.
Load temporally-binned image stacks in ImFCS 1.52 plugin.
Set frame time, bleach correction, and intensity filter values in the plugin.
Load a dark image with the same dimensions as the measurement image for background correction.
Select “G1” mode in the “N&B tab.
Press the “N&B button in “N&B analysis to generate N&B maps.
Temporarily bin the image stacks using the Average bin method.
Choose the "SRRF analysis" option in NanoJ-SRRF plugin and set desired parameters for ring radius, radiality magnification, axes in ring, display_mode, and temporal analysis mode.
Click "OK" to generate SRRF images.
For SOFI images, follow the same steps but use minimum values for ring radius, radiality magnification, and axes in ring.
Temporally bin the image stacks to generate single time-averaged images.
Load the images into Huygens Professional.
Set the microscope type to confocal.
Set the X, Y and Z sampling intervals to the ideal Nyquist value.
Set the optical parameters according to the microscopy system used: NA, refractive indices of lens immersion oil and embedding medium, objective quality.
Set the channel parameters: backprojected pinhole = maximum allowed value, excitation wavelength, emission wavelength, excitation fill factor = 2.
The theoretical PSF will be automatically generated.
Use a suitable deconvolution algorithm. e.g., Classic Maximum Likelihood Estimation (CMLE).
The deconvolved image will be generated.
